name: Movement Disorders / Parkinson's Disease Center
description: Parkinson's disease, essential tremor, dystonia, atypical parkinsonism, functional movement disorders, and related conditions. Also handles Botox injections and Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) evaluations.
intake_requirements: Patient must have been previously evaluated by a PCP or other specialist before referral. Last 3 clinical notes and MRI reports required. Some diagnoses require referral triage review before scheduling.
age_restrictions: Adults (18+). Pediatric movement disorders may route to Kennedy Krieger Institute.
do_not_route_here: Huntington's Disease — route to Huntington's Disease Center
Acute unilateral weakness — route to Cerebrovascular
Concussion or TBI — route to PM&R

name: Epilepsy Center
description: New and established epilepsy, first-time seizures, drug-resistant epilepsy, epilepsy surgery evaluation, dietary therapy for seizures, and neurostimulator management.
intake_requirements: Last 3 clinical notes + MRI and EEG reports. Records required at least 14 days before appointment for general epilepsy. First-time seizure pathway available for new-onset seizures within the last 14 days.
urgency_flags: first seizure within the last 14 days
age_restrictions: Adults (18+) for adult epilepsy center. Pediatric epilepsy has separate pathway.
do_not_route_here: Syncope — route to Cardiology first
TIA / episodic unilateral weakness — route to Cerebrovascular
Dizziness without seizure features — route to Vestibular or General Neurology

name: Stroke and Cerebrovascular Neurology
description: Stroke, TIA, cerebrovascular disease, vascular malformations, carotid disease, and related vascular conditions affecting the brain and spinal cord.
conditions: Sickle Cell Disease with Stroke or TIA
intake_requirements: Referring physician note + MRI/MRA and CT or cerebrovascular angiograms. Upload imaging to portal. Records needed at least 7 days before appointment. Some presentations require referral triage review.
urgency_flags: episodic unilateral weakness in patient with vascular risk factors
sudden onset worst headache of life
age_restrictions: Adults (18+) for adult cerebrovascular. Pediatric stroke routes to Dr. Lisa Sun.
do_not_route_here: Aneurysm/AVM not seen by neurosurgeon — route to Neurosurgery first
Memory loss not related to stroke — route to Memory Center
Memory loss after concussion — route to PM&R
Ataxia due to stroke — still route here, not Ataxia Center

name: Headache Center
description: All primary headache disorders including migraine, cluster headache, trigeminal neuralgia, and refractory daily headache.
intake_requirements: Adult Headache Questionnaire must be sent to patient and returned before appointment. Records faxed at least 7 days prior. Cannot prescribe opioids or benzodiazepines.
urgency_flags: thunderclap headache (worst headache of life, sudden onset) — rule out SAH before routing
headache with fever and stiff neck
age_restrictions: Adult Headache Center (18+). Pediatric Headache Center for patients under 18.
do_not_route_here: Concussion or traumatic brain injury — route to PM&R
Thunderclap headache — urgent, rule out SAH first
Patient currently on opioids/benzodiazepines who will not taper — denied

name: Multiple Sclerosis and Neuroimmunology
description: Multiple sclerosis, demyelinating diseases, autoimmune neurological conditions, neuromyelitis optica, transverse myelitis, and neuroinfectious diseases.
intake_requirements: Patient must have been previously evaluated by a neurologist or ophthalmologist. MRI of brain and spine required before scheduling. CSF results and relevant labwork if available. Records required 7 days before appointment.
age_restrictions: Adults (18+) for adult neuroimmunology. Pediatric neuroimmunology has separate pathway.
do_not_route_here: Patient without prior neurologist or ophthalmologist evaluation — denied
Patient without MRI confirming diagnosis — denied
Ataxia due to MS — route here, not Ataxia Center
Myelopathy of vascular or structural cause — route to Cerebrovascular or Neurosurgery

name: Neuromuscular Medicine (Drachman Division)
description: ALS, myasthenia gravis, peripheral neuropathy, myopathy, muscular dystrophy, CIDP, Guillain-Barré syndrome, and related neuromuscular conditions.
intake_requirements: Last 3 clinical notes + MRI + relevant labwork + genetic testing if applicable + EMG/NCS results. EMG is required for most neuropathy and myopathy referrals before scheduling. Motor neuron disease and SMA may be scheduled without EMG. Records reviewed within 7-10 business days.
age_restrictions: Adults (18+). Pediatric neuromuscular has separate pathway.
do_not_route_here: Acute unilateral weakness — route to Cerebrovascular (TIA)
Episodic weakness fully resolving in minutes — route to Cerebrovascular
Spinal cord disease from MS — route to Neuroimmunology
Patient without EMG (for neuropathy/myopathy) — will be denied, request EMG first

name: Sleep Neurology
description: Neurologically-based sleep disorders including narcolepsy, REM sleep behavior disorder, restless legs syndrome, and insomnia not managed by pulmonary sleep.
conditions: Insomnia (not previously managed by Pulmonary Sleep)
Obstructive Sleep Apnea (if new to Hopkins sleep services)
intake_requirements: Last 3 clinical notes + all previous sleep studies. Records required 7 days before appointment. Cannot prescribe opioids or benzodiazepines.
age_restrictions: Adults (18+). Pediatric sleep has separate pathway via HCMA.
do_not_route_here: Patient previously seen by Pulmonary Sleep — return to Pulmonary Sleep
CPAP/BiPAP management — route to Pulmonary Sleep or HCMA Sleep Lab
Sleep study scheduling — route to HCMA Sleep Lab directly

name: Cognitive Neurology / Memory Center
description: Alzheimer's disease, dementia, mild cognitive impairment, and memory disorders. Age determines routing between Memory Center and Young-Onset Dementias Clinic.
intake_requirements: Last 3 clinical notes + MRI + labwork + genetic testing if applicable.
age_restrictions: Memory Center: age 55 or older. Young-Onset Dementias Clinic: under 55 (call 410-955-5147). Frontotemporal Dementia (FTD) routes to Young-Onset Dementias Clinic regardless of age.
do_not_route_here: Memory loss that began after stroke — route to Cerebrovascular
Memory loss that began after concussion/TBI — route to PM&R
Huntington's Disease — route to Huntington's Disease Center (410-955-2398)
Lewy Body Dementia — route to Movement Disorders

name: Vestibular and Neuro-Visual Disorders
description: Chronic dizziness, vertigo, nystagmus, diplopia, and visual disturbances of neurological origin.
intake_requirements: Clinical notes + visual, vestibular, or audiology testing + MRI/MRA. Two appointments may be required: first for vestibular function testing, second with neurologist. Referral triage review required for some presentations. Records required 7 days before appointment.
urgency_flags: sudden onset vision loss — rule out stroke
acute vestibular syndrome with new MRI lesion
age_restrictions: Adults (18+). Pediatric nystagmus has separate pathway.
do_not_route_here: BPPV (Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo) — route to PM&R
Vision loss with stroke concern — route to Cerebrovascular
Meniere's Disease — route to Otolaryngology
Dizziness < 6 months with stroke concern — route to Cerebrovascular

name: Ataxia Center
description: Cerebellar and spinocerebellar ataxias, hereditary ataxia, and isolated gait ataxia of non-stroke, non-MS origin.
intake_requirements: Last 3 clinical notes + MRI + genetic testing results if applicable. Records required 21 days before appointment. Record review required — up to 14 business days for response.
age_restrictions: Adults (18+). Ataxia Telangiectasia routes to ATCC (410-614-1922). Friedreich's Ataxia routes to MDA (410-955-6435).
do_not_route_here: Ataxia due to stroke — route to Cerebrovascular
Ataxia due to MS — route to Neuroimmunology
Ataxia Telangiectasia — route to ATCC
Friedreich's Ataxia — route to MDA

name: General Neurology
description: Undifferentiated neurological presentations that do not clearly fit a subspecialty, and conditions requiring initial neurological evaluation.
conditions: Back / Neck Pain with neurological symptoms
key_symptoms: symptoms not clearly fitting one subspecialty
intake_requirements: Relevant clinical notes and any diagnostic testing if applicable. Prior PCP or specialist evaluation required. If symptoms began within 4 weeks, may qualify for expedited scheduling.
do_not_route_here: Presentations that clearly fit a subspecialty — use the appropriate subspecialty clinic
Patient without prior PCP or specialist evaluation — return to PCP first
